questions.stem: At time $t=0$, a particle is projected vertically upwards with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point 10 m above the ground. At time $T$ seconds, the particle hits the ground with speed $17.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Find

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $v=u+at \Rightarrow 17.5=-10.5+9.8T$ M1 A1 f.t.
$T=2\tfrac{6}{7}$ (s) DM1 A1 (4)
Alternatives for (b):
Way 2: $s=\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)T \Rightarrow 10=\left(\frac{17.5+(-10.5)}{2}\right)T$ M1 A1 f.t.
$\frac{20}{7}=T$ DM1 A1 (4)
OR: $s=ut+\tfrac{1}{2}at^2 \Rightarrow -10=10.5t-4.9t^2$ M1 A1 f.t.
Leading to $T=2\tfrac{6}{7}, \left(-\tfrac{5}{7}\right)$, rejecting negative DM1 A1 (4)
(b) can be done independently of (a):
$s=vt-\tfrac{1}{2}at^2 \Rightarrow -10=-17.5t+4.9t^2$ M1 A1
Leading to $T=2\tfrac{6}{7}, \tfrac{5}{7}$ DM1
For final A1, second solution has to be rejected. $\tfrac{5}{7}$ leads to a negative $u$. A1 (4)

The time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$ is 90 s and $AB=1410$ m.

(2)

The time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$ is 90 s and $AB=1410$ m.
(a) Sketch, in the space below, a speed-time graph to show the motion of the car from $A$ to $B$.
(2)

questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) [shape of speed-time graph: constant speed 25 for 30 s, uniform deceleration to 10, then constant 10 until t=90] B1 shape

questions.stem:
Two forces $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ act on a particle at a point $O$. The force $\mathbf{P}$ has magnitude 15 N and the force $\mathbf{Q}$ has magnitude $X$ newtons. The angle between $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ is $150^\circ$, as shown in Figure 1. The resultant of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ is $\mathbf{R}$.

Given that the angle between $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ is $50^\circ$, find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $(\uparrow)$ $15\sin30^\circ=R\sin50^\circ$ M1 A1
$R\approx9.79\,(\mathrm{N})$ DM1 A1 (4)
Alternatives using sine rule in (a) or (b); cosine rule in (b):
Way 2: $\dfrac{R}{\sin30^\circ}=\dfrac{15}{\sin50^\circ}$ M1 A1
$R\approx9.79\,(\mathrm{N})$ DM1 A1 (4)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $(\rightarrow)$ $X-15\cos30^\circ=R\cos50^\circ$, ft their $R$ M1 A2 ft
$X\approx19.3\,(\mathrm{N})$ DM1 A1 (5)
Alternatives:
Way 2: $\dfrac{X}{\sin100^\circ}=\dfrac{15}{\sin50^\circ}=\dfrac{R}{\sin30^\circ}$, ft on $R$ M1 A2 ft on $R$
$X\approx19.3\,(\mathrm{N})$ DM1 A1 (5)
OR: cosine rule; any of $R^2=X^2+15^2-2\times15\times X\cos30^\circ$, $15^2=R^2+X^2-2\times X\times R\cos50^\circ$: $X^2=R^2+15^2-2\times15\times R\cos100^\circ$, ft on $R$ M1 A2 ft on $R$
$X\approx19.3\,(\mathrm{N})$ DM1 A1 (5)

questions.stem: A package of mass 4 kg lies on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The package is held in equilibrium by a force of magnitude 45 N acting at an angle of $50^\circ$ to the plane, as shown in Figure 3. The force is acting in a vertical plane through a line of greatest slope of the plane. The package is in equilibrium on the point of moving up the plane. The package is modelled as a particle. Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the magnitude of the normal reaction of the plane on the package,
(5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the coefficient of friction between the plane and the package.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Use of $F=\mu R$ M1
$F+4g\sin30^\circ=45\cos50^\circ$ M1 A2 (1,0)
Leading to $\mu\approx0.14$ (accept 0.136) DM1 A1 (6)

questions.stem: Two particles $P$ and $Q$, of mass 2 kg and 3 kg respectively, are joined by a light inextensible string. Initially the particles are at rest on a rough horizontal plane with the string taut. A constant force $\mathbf{F}$ of magnitude 30 N is applied to $Q$ in the direction $PQ$, as shown in Figure 4. The force is applied for 3 s and during this time $Q$ travels a distance of 6 m. The coefficient of friction between each particle and the plane is $\mu$. Find

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) N2L for system: $30-\mu5g=5a$, ft their $a$, accept symbol M1 A1ft
$\mu=\dfrac{14}{3g}=\dfrac{10}{21}$ or awrt 0.48 DM1 A1 (4)

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) N2L for $P$: $T-\mu2g=2a$, ft their $\mu$, their $a$, accept symbols M1 A1 ft
$T-\dfrac{14}{3g}\times2g=2\times\dfrac{4}{3}$
Leading to $T=12\,(\mathrm{N})$, awrt 12 DM1 A1 (4)
Alternatively: N2L for $Q$: $30-T-\mu3g=3a$ M1 A1
Leading to $T=12\,(\mathrm{N})$, awrt 12 DM1 A1
